info.title: Subako Public API
info.description:
The public HTTP interface to Subako.

Every request carries a bearer credential, and the organization it acts in is the credential's -- no path names one. Work resources belong to a workspace, named by the `Kikuvi-Workspace` header where a user credential cannot imply one.

Listings are cursor paged: pass the `next_cursor` a page returns back as `after`, and `order` decides which way the walk continues; pass its `prev_cursor` back as `before` to step back. Writes that create something accept an `Idempotency-Key`, and a retry under the same key returns the saved receipt rather than acting twice.

get.description:
The same log as a live tail, framed as server-sent events: one event per row, `id` the seq, `event` the wire `type`, and `data` the same `SessionEventBody` the paged read renders.

The stream stays open across idle stretches -- a keep-alive comment holds the connection while nothing happens -- so one connection spans a session's whole life rather than a single run. With no position named it starts at the live head, fixed before the response begins; a client that wants history pages the events route newest-first and deduplicates on seq against what the tail delivers.

With `deltas=true` the stream also carries `delta` frames: a model's output as it is produced, one `SessionDeltaBody` each, with no `id`. Deltas are never stored and may be lost; each previews one target until the event that ends it lands -- for a model call, the `message_assistant` with the same `model_call_id` -- or a `discard` frame says it never will. A reader joining mid-target first receives the frames that target sent so far.

Subsequent events carry the seq as their id, the wire type as their event name, and one SessionEventBody as their data. SessionSandboxStatusBody.description:
Stable lifecycle vocabulary for v1. Adding or changing a value requires a
new API version; additional internal states map to these public states.

- `dormant`: no instance has been started; an exec provisions one.
- `provisioning`: an instance is starting, restoring, or resuming; exec waits.
- `running`: an instance is available for exec.
- `draining`: backup, suspension, or retirement is in progress; exec waits.
- `suspended`: an idle instance is paused; an exec resumes it. Archive deletion
  still returns 409 until automatic retirement.
- `archived`: the instance is retired; an exec provisions a new one and restores
  the last published archive, if present. Archive deletion is permitted.
- `failed`: the generation failed; a new exec attempts provisioning from the
  last published archive, if present. Archive deletion is permitted.

A published archive can be downloaded in any state. Status is a snapshot;
a concurrent exec or lifecycle transition can change whether deletion succeeds.

byte_hours.description: Bytes held times hours held, rounded down.

StorageSummaryBody.description:
Storage held, archives and volumes together, by how it was priced. A
class with none is absent.

unrated.description: Storage a charge was due for but no rate priced.

SubmitKindBody.description: What the input did to the session.

SubmitOutcomeBody.description: The run the input landed in, and whether it started that run or joined it.

TokenEndpointAuthBody.description:
How Subako authenticates at the provider's token endpoint as this client
(RFC 7591 §2): `none` for a public client, which PKCE alone proves, or the
client secret in the form or in a `Basic` header.

TokenEndpointAuthMethodBody.description: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint, without its secret.

TokenTotalsBody.description:
Token counts summed per format, each field on its own: the formats count
different things, so they are never added together. A format with no
calls is absent.

ToolDescriptorBody.description: One tool, named as the model sees it.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the tool's arguments.

ToolRuleBody.description: Per-tool override; `name` is the exact tool name the source reports.

UpdateModelProviderBody.description:
An absent field leaves that part of the provider as it stands, so a
rename need not restate the endpoint -- nor the credential.

api_key.description:
A new upstream key, sealed and put in place of the stored credential:
shorthand for an `api_key` auth. Write-only: no route answers with a
key, so there is nothing to read back and nothing to compare against.

oneOf.description:
A new auth, put in place of the stored one whole: a new key, a new
role, or a switch between the two. The provider keeps its id, so every
agent version already naming it goes on resolving. Send this or
`api_key`, not both.

UpdateOAuthClientBody.description:
An absent field leaves that part of the client as it stands; a present
list replaces the stored one whole, so an empty one clears it. A present
`token_endpoint_auth` replaces the method and the secret together. The
endpoints and `client_id` are fixed at creation, so a body naming one is
refused rather than read past.

UpdateVaultBody.description:
An absent field leaves that part of the vault as it stands, so a rename
need not restate the metadata. Only `external_id` takes `null`, which
removes it; a `null` name or metadata is refused rather than read as absent.

external_id.description: A new external id, or `null` to remove it.

metadata.description:
Replaces every label the vault has, under the bounds
`CreateVaultBody.metadata` states.

UsageBillingBody.description:
How a row was priced. `rated`: a charge landed with it, which `cost` names.
`byok`: a call through the workspace's own model provider, which is never
charged. `unrated`: a charge was due but no rate priced it.

Stable vocabulary for v1: adding a value requires a new API version.

accounted_at.description:
The instant the row counts toward, which `starting_at` and `ending_at`
filter on: `occurred_at`, unless the row was recorded after the usage
report had already finalized that instant.

cost.description:
Hundred-millionths of a credit, as `balance`. Absent for a byok call
or a platform one nothing priced.

metadata.description:
The metadata of the session the row was spent in, copied when it was
recorded.

UsageReportBody.description: One page of a usage report.

finalized_before.description:
A row whose `ending_at` is at or before this instant is final and
never changes again; a later one may still grow. Null until any usage
is final.

items.description:
Ordered by `starting_at`, then by each `group_by` value in turn,
bytewise, with no value last. A combination with no usage has no row.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `after`, with the same other parameters, for the next page;
null on the last.

UsageReportRowBody.description:
The usage in one bucket for one combination of `group_by` values. Only
the dimensions grouped by appear; one with no value for the row, such as
the model of a sandbox's run time, is null.

kind.description:
The usage kind, such as `llm_tokens` or `storage`. An open
vocabulary: a kind Subako starts measuring later arrives under its
own name, so a client keeps a value it does not know rather than
rejecting the row.

oneOf.description: The engine's time on one claim interval of the run.
A sandbox's time on one running interval.

Bytes held over one interval: a published workspace archive, or a
session tree's volume, billed to its root.
The worker's time on one function call.

grant.description: The grant the call went through, as the agent's config names it.

oneOf.description:
Bytes written to a session tree's volume, as billed: by a function
call, which `run_id`, `grant`, and `tool` name, or by an upload, which
leaves them absent.

UsageResourceBody.description: What an event measured; `kind` names the shape.

UsageSummaryBody.description:
What a row's usage came to, kind by kind. A kind with no usage is absent,
and a kind added later arrives as a field of its own, which a client that
does not know it ignores.

cost.description: Hundred-millionths of a credit: every `rated` cost below, summed.

VaultBody.description:
A vault row. Carries no credential and no envelope: a vault is a
container, and what is in it is read through the credential route.

external_id.description: The caller's own name for the vault, or `null` when it has none.

VaultCreated.description: The id of the vault just created. Read it back for the rest of its row.

VaultCredentialCheckedDetails.description: A credential was tried against its server, which may refresh it or mark it for reconnecting.

VaultCredentialCreatedDetails.description: A credential was created in a vault.

VaultCredentialReconnectedDetails.description: A credential was reauthorized through OAuth.

VaultCredentialUsedDetails.description: A run used a vault credential, the first time it did. The actor is whoever sent the message that started the run.

VaultDeletedDetails.description: A vault was deleted, with its credentials.

VersionPinBody.description: The latest version at resolution time, or an exact one.

VolumeAreaParam.description:
One of a volume's two areas: `tmp`, always there and cleared a day after the
tree's last activity, or `data`, kept until the root session is deleted where
the root agent enables it.

VolumeConfigBody.description: The roots the session tree's functions reach beyond `/volume/tmp`.

VolumeDataBody.description:
Whether the volume offers a persistent `/volume/data` root. `enabled`
mounts it for the session tree's functions.

modified.description: When the entry itself last changed, in UTC.

path.description: The entry's path in the area, e.g. `notes/a.txt`.

size.description: Bytes for a file; 0 for a directory or a symlink.

VolumeFileDeletedDetails.description: A file was deleted from a session's volume.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `after` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

truncated.description: True when another page follows, which `next_cursor` then starts.

path.description: The file's path in the area.

VolumeFileWrittenDetails.description: A file was written to a session's volume. Its path and content stay in the volume.

VolumeListDepthParam.description:
How far beneath its prefix a listing reads: `all` for every entry beneath
it, `children` for only those directly in it.

VolumeWriteSummaryBody.description:
Bytes written to volumes by how they were priced. A class with none is
absent.

unrated.description: Bytes a charge was due for but no rate priced.

oneOf.description: A pick among options the agent writes.
Free text.
Yes or no.

A widget the app declares. A client without a renderer for `id`
lets the person tell the agent so.

answer.description: The JSON Schema an answer must match.

description.description: What the model reads to choose the widget.

id.description:
The renderer's key. A change to `props` or `answer` that would
break a client takes a new id.

props.description: The JSON Schema of what the agent fills in.

WidgetGrantBody.description:
One widget a form may use: a built-in every Subako surface draws, or a
`custom` one the app's own clients draw from its id.

WorkloadIdentityBody.description:
What to register in a cloud account, and what to trust there, for this
workspace's providers to authenticate as the workspace.

issuer.description:
The OpenID Connect issuer every workspace token names. Register it as
an identity provider in your cloud account or your OpenAI
organization, or as a federation issuer in your Anthropic
organization; its discovery document is at
`{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

subject.description:
The `sub` claim of this workspace's tokens, and of no other
workspace's: the value a role's trust policy, a federation rule's
`subject_prefix`, or an OpenAI mapping's `sub` pins.

WorkspaceBody.description:
A workspace: the scope agents, sessions, vaults, skills, and keys
belong to.

WorkspaceDeletedDetails.description: A workspace was deleted, with everything in it.

WorkspaceMemberAddedDetails.description: A member was added to a workspace.

WorkspaceMemberBody.description: One member of a workspace, with the role they hold in it.

WorkspaceMemberRemovedDetails.description: A member was removed from a workspace.

orphaned_api_keys.description: Live API keys the member created in the workspace, which keep working.

WorkspaceMemberRoleSetDetails.description: A member's role in a workspace changed.

WorkspaceRoleBody.description:
What a member may do in the workspace. An admin manages the workspace and
its membership; a member works in it.
